definition: A binding contract provision — typically buried in Helix Biosystems geneware agreements — that grants the issuing company partial intellectual property rights over any biological modifications made to the signatory's genome. Enforced through proprietary kill-switch sequences embedded in the modification itself.
origin: Corporate legal jargon from Helix Biosystems standard service contracts, circa 2170s.
usage: Used by lawyers, geneware black marketeers warning clients, and activists fighting synthetic personhood legislation.
example: She didn't read the fine print — three years later Helix invoked the helix clause and locked her enhanced vision until she settled.
